findings.evidence: `theorem integral_congr {a b : ℝ} (h : EqOn f g [[a, b]]) : ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a..b, g x ∂μ` at mathlib/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/IntervalIntegral/Basic.lean:1079.
findings.fix: Use the dedicated congruence lemma: `exact intervalIntegral.integral_congr fun x _ => by simp only [...]; ring` (or `intervalIntegral.integral_congr_ae`).
findings.issue: `congr 1 with x` inside the local `key` descends into the unfolded definition of `intervalIntegral` (a difference of two `setIntegral`s); which subgoals it produces depends on `congr`'s heuristics and on how `intervalIntegral` is spelled, so the step can break silently on an upstream refactor.

findings.evidence: Both `have`s are `integral_congr_ae (ae_of_all _ fun x => …)` over integrands that are equal as polynomial products; lines 156 and 202.
findings.fix: Add one private lemma `integral_eval_mul_eval_congr {p₁ q₁ p₂ q₂ : ℝ[X]} (h : p₁ * q₁ = p₂ * q₂) : ∫ x, p₁.eval x * q₁.eval x ∂gegenbauerThreeHalvesMeasure = ∫ x, p₂.eval x * q₂.eval x ∂…` proved by `integral_congr_ae`, then discharge `hcomm` with `mul_comm _ _` and `hX` with `by ring`.
findings.issue: The same reusable fact — that the weighted pairing only depends on the product polynomial — is inlined twice as bulky `have` blocks: `hcomm` (lines 153-156, `∫ Cₙ Cₘ = ∫ Cₘ Cₙ`) and `hX` (lines 198-202, `∫ (X Cₙ₊₂) Cₙ₊₁ = ∫ (X Cₙ₊₁) Cₙ₊₂`). Milestones 4-6 will need it again.

findings.evidence: `C_eq_natCast` is `C (n : R) = (n : R[X])` (mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Polynomial/Basic.lean:467); by contrast `one_sub_X_sq_mul_derivative_gegenbauerThreeHalves` (line 303) needs no such preamble because its `C` coefficients already match as atoms.
findings.fix: Add a one-line comment at the first occurrence (e.g. `-- push `C` through sums/products to `natCast` so `linear_combination` sees matching atoms`) and reference it at the later ones.
findings.issue: The `simp only [C_add, C_mul, C_eq_natCast, C_ofNat, C_1, …] at … ⊢` preamble appears four times (lines 262, 281, 320, and implicitly via `C_ofNat` at 331) with no comment. It is not simplification: it is required so `linear_combination`'s `ring` can cancel `C ((n:R)+2)` against the expanded `(n : R[X]) + 2` instead of treating `C _` as an opaque atom. A reader cannot tell why the step is there or why it may be dropped.

summary: Proofs are mostly robust `linear_combination`/`simp`-driven scripts with no `change`/`show` and no long scripts, but two integral-rearrangement steps are inlined twice instead of factored, one of them uses the fragile `congr 1` on an interval integral, and the repeated `C`-normalisation preamble before `linear_combination` is undocumented.
